label: Connectedness and Orthogonality — unseen mastery test

items.stem: A connected block design guarantees that:
options: All treatment contrasts are estimable after adjusting for blocks
Every pair occurs in exactly λ blocks
items.explanation: Connectedness is an estimability property.

items.stem: The treatment concurrence graph has:
options: Treatments as vertices; shared-block pairs joined by edges
items.explanation: Vertices represent treatments and edges represent pair concurrence.

items.stem: For v treatments, the connectedness rank condition is:
items.explanation: There are v−1 independent treatment contrasts.

items.stem: A path 1–2–3–4 makes the four-treatment concurrence graph:
items.explanation: A path links every vertex.

items.stem: Orthogonality of centred contrast spaces means:
items.explanation: Zero cross-products define orthogonality.

items.stem: In a complete RBD, treatment contrasts are orthogonal to:
items.explanation: Every treatment appears once in each block.

items.stem: A design has v=5 treatments and rank(C)=4. Is it connected? Enter 1 for yes, 0 for no.
items.explanation: The required rank is v−1=4, so it is connected.

items.stem: For v=8 treatments, what rank must C have for connectedness?
items.explanation: Connectedness requires rank(C)=v−1=7.

items.stem: A design has v=6 treatments and rank(C)=4. How many connected components does its concurrence graph have under the standard incidence model?
items.explanation: For c components, rank(C)=v−c; c=6−4=2.

items.stem: A design can be connected without being a BIBD because:
options: Every pair must share a block
A path can connect treatments even when pair concurrence differs
items.explanation: Connectedness requires paths, not equal concurrence for every pair.

items.stem: In a Latin square, treatment contrasts are orthogonal to:
items.explanation: The balanced row and column incidence gives orthogonality.

items.stem: For equal block size k, K in C=R−NK⁻¹N′ is:
items.explanation: Equal block sizes make the block-size diagonal matrix K=kI.

items.stem: A design has v=10 treatments and 3 connected components. Find rank(C).
A BIBD has v=7 and λ=1. What is the number of edges in its complete concurrence graph?
items.explanation: A complete graph on 7 vertices has 7×6/2=21 edges.

items.stem: Which statements about connectedness are correct?
items.explanation: A, B and C are correct; direct adjacency for every pair is not required.
statements: All v−1 independent treatment contrasts are estimable.
A connected concurrence graph has one component.
A path can connect two treatments that never share a block directly.
Every pair must occur together in at least one block.

B.why: A connected graph has one component.

D.why: Direct adjacency for every pair is unnecessary.

items.stem: Which statements about orthogonality are correct?
items.explanation: Zero centred cross-products define orthogonality; complete RBD and Latin square provide standard examples.
statements: Orthogonal centred contrast spaces have zero cross-products.
Complete RBD treatment contrasts are orthogonal to block contrasts.
Latin-square treatment contrasts are orthogonal to row and column contrasts.
Orthogonality and connectedness mean exactly the same thing.

B.why: Each treatment occurs once in every block.

C.why: Each treatment occurs once per row and column.

items.stem: Which statements about C=R−NK⁻¹N′ are correct?
items.explanation: C is v×v; equal block size gives K=kI; connectedness requires rank v−1.
statements: If all blocks have size k, K=kI.
The design is connected iff rank(C)=v−1.
The connectedness rank condition is rank(C)=v.

A.why: There are v treatment rows and columns.

B.why: K stores block sizes on its diagonal.

C.why: All independent treatment contrasts must be estimable.

D.why: The grand-mean direction is not a treatment contrast.

items.stem: A complete concurrence graph has 5 treatments. How many edges does it have?
items.explanation: A complete graph on v vertices has v(v−1)/2 edges: 5×4/2=10.

items.stem: A connected design has v=9 treatments. What is rank(C)?
items.explanation: For a connected design, rank(C)=v−1=8.

items.stem: A design has v=8 treatments and rank(C)=5. How many connected components does its concurrence graph have?
items.explanation: For c components, rank(C)=v−c, so c=8−5=3.
